name: Rhode Island - Single filer with TDI
description: Single person earning $75,000 annually in Rhode Island, exercising the RI TDI (state disability insurance) contribution

sources.description: Calculated using 2026 IRS tax brackets (Rev. Proc. 2025-32) and RI DLT 2026 TDI rate
sources.notes: Federal: std deduction $16,100, taxable $58,900, tax 10%*$12,400=$1,240+12%*$38,000=$4,560+22%*$8,500=$1,870=$7,670. RI state tax figure ($2,393) uses this config's existing RI brackets/std-deduction params as-is; a wide tolerance (+/-15 abs or +/-0.001 x gross) is used since RI's exact 2026 state bracket figures were not independently re-verified as part of this SDI-focused vector. SS: $75,000*6.2%=$4,650. Medicare: $75,000*1.45%=$1,087.50. Additional Medicare: $0 (below $200k). TDI: $75,000*1.1%=$825.00 (RI 2026 wage base is $100,000; $75,000 is under the cap).

sources.description: RI Department of Labor & Training - 2026 TDI tax rate (1.1%) and taxable wage base ($100,000), down from 1.3% / $89,200 in 2025
sources.notes: TDI contribution rate 1.1% for CY2026 on a taxable wage base of $100,000 (max annual employee contribution $1,100).
